subject: Dashboard telemetry convergence: request for per-route cost vs latency alignment
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Alice <alice@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Dashboard telemetry convergence: request for per-route cost vs latency alignment

Team —

Following the Acme Health onboarding call yesterday, a few gaps came up where our Console shows per-route token costs but the latency breakdown is only surface-level (p50/p95 for the endpoint). Acme wants a single pane where they can:

- See cost/kg (per-route cost normalized by traffic slice) aligned with tail latency percentiles by model variant.
- Fastly identify which routes incur high token cost *and* high tail latency so they can triage model/config choices.
- Be able to attribute spikes to customer slices (tenant / prompt-type) and then open a ticket from the dashboard.

Proposed short spec:
1) Add a per-route card that shows side-by-side: tokens/1000 (cost proxy), p50/p95/p99 latency, and percent of requests with KV-cache hits.
2) Wire a drill-down to sample traces and last-request tokens for the selected time window.
3) Surface the recommended action: cache policy tweak, batching hint, or alternate model variant with projected cost delta.

I've attached a one-pager and a rough wireframe for an MVP. Can we talk feasibility and an expected timeline? If it's heavy on infra, let's scope a partial MVP that surfaces the cost/latency alignment using our existing metrics store.

Thanks —
Grace
Grace O'Connor
Product Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: telemetry-convergence-proposal.pdf (PDF, 210kb), mvp-wireframe.png (image, 480x320)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Dashboard telemetry convergence: request for per-route cost vs latency alignment

Grace —

Quick feasibility notes from infra/telemetry: we already emit per-request token_count and latencies to the metrics pipeline but the big gap is tenant/route cardinality in the TSDB. Two approaches:

A) Pre-aggregate at ingestion keyed by route_id + tenant_bucket (cheap on read, more ingestion cost).
B) Do on-the-fly joins in the analytics layer for low-volume queries (slower for big windows).

For an MVP I recommend B to keep infra changes minimal — we can limit query window to 7 days and add sampling. That gets us the side-by-side card with a small perf hit on heavy queries.

I'll scope a rough effort: engineering spike (2d) to validate query plan, then 3 sprints for a minimal UI + backend pagination. If Acme needs it in <6 weeks we should consider a concierge-run export for them (we can produce a CSV on-demand).

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Engineering Manager, Platform

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 15:40:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Dashboard telemetry convergence: request for per-route cost vs latency alignment

We should also tie this into SLO owner metadata and existing alerting. A couple of practical considerations:

- If the per-route card recommends a fallback (cheaper model variant) we must show the expected latency delta and the current SLO impact.
- For sampling, preserve the request-level KV-cache flag and model_variant string — otherwise the recommendations will be noisy.
- We need a short list of acceptable fallbacks per model family; ops will not accept an automated swap without an owner.

Happy to take ownership of the SLO mapping piece. Also +1 to Karthik's B MVP approach so we can iterate.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Reliability

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Alice <alice@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Dashboard telemetry convergence: request for per-route cost vs latency alignment

Looping in a short note for Acme — we can include a tenant-level cost slice and a knob to toggle sampling based on traffic percent. For privacy/compliance, we'll ensure sampled payloads exclude PII.

Alice — is Acme comfortable with a sampled trace approach for the MVP, or do you need 100% fidelity for the first 30 days? We can provide full exports under a concierge arrangement if required.

Vanessa Ortiz
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

On Thu, Jun 11, 2026 at 08:03 AM Alice <alice@acmehealth.com> wrote:
> Grace / team — this sounds promising. For the pilot we are OK with sampling as long as the sampling is stratified by customer app and prompt-type. We want to be able to see whether particular prompt flows (e.g., triage workflows) are responsible for the cost/latency skew.
> 
> Also can you add a linkable action that opens a support ticket pre-filled with the selected time range and tenant? That would speed up escalation.
> 
> Thanks,
> Alice
> Director of Platform Engineering, Acme Health

Thanks everyone — good alignment. Recap and next steps: 

1) Karthik: engineering spike (2d) to validate analytics-layer join and sample-based query performance (target: complete by Jun 15).
2) Markus: map SLOs to model families and provide the fallback whitelist for UI recommendations (target: Jun 18).
3) Vanessa: confirm sampling design and privacy checklist with Acme; confirm whether they want concierge exports for first 30 days (target: Jun 14).
4) Grace: draft the Console card copy and acceptance criteria; create JIRA ticket OBS-9482 and link design doc.

Action: I'll schedule a 30-min sync for Monday (Jun 15) to review the spike results. If anyone needs the wireframes or the one-pager, see: https://docs.redwood.ai/obs/telemetry-convergence-draft

Grace
